newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst division to become subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst division to become subsidiary.

text.p: German chemicals group Hoechst AG said on Monday it would transform its diagnostics division into a separate legal entity as part of a continuing management reorganisation.
With effect from January 1, 1997 Hoechst's diagnostics business will be run by a new subsidiary, wholly-owned Behring Diagnostics GmbH, Hoechst said in a statement.
The unit's managing director will be Uwe Bicker, with Friedhelm Blobel in charge of research, development and production and Reiner Gleiss heading finance, personnel and administration.
The diagnostics division will in 1996 generate about one billion marks in sales and make an operating profit of about 95 million marks, Hoechst said.

Behring Diagnostics is one of Hoechst's four life science divisions, the others being drugs subsidiary Hoechst Marion Roussel, veterinary chemicals unit Hoechst Roussel Vet and plant protection unit Agrevo.
